newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland says 14 applications for Rockall oil licences.
newsitem.headline: Ireland says 14 applications for Rockall oil licences.

text.p: A total of nine groups submitted 14 applications for 16-year frontier exploration licences to prospect for oil in the Rockall Trough off Ireland's west coast, Ireland's Energy Department said on Thursday.
"Seventeen different exploration companies are involved in the bids," Minister of State at the Department of Transport, Energy and Communications Emmet Stagg said.

The awards, which are expected to be announced in early June, were submitted for 58 blocks or part blocks in the Rockall Trough by the close of the Petroleum Exploration Licensing round in the area on Wednesday, the Energy Department said in a statement on Thursday.

"It is my intention and that of the government that the exploration of the Irish offshore should be promoted and encouraged to the greatest possible extent to enhance the prospects of obtaining further commercial discoveries," Stagg said.
Stagg confirmed that the Porcupine Basin, which was the subject of a Frontier Licensing Round in 1995, would remain closed until further notice.
He said he was closing a further area adjoining the south of the Porcupine Basin and an area covering the Seven Heads oil and gas accumulation to the southwest of the Kinsale Head gas field.
"I will issue a statement of my intentions in regard to the future of both areas after awards of licences in the Rockall Trough," Stagg said.

A substantial number of major international oil companies were expected to apply for the licences which cover an area of 150,000 square kilometres. The acreage includes 615 full blocks and 35 part blocks.
Statoil, Texaco Inc, Marathon Oil, Total SA and Enterprise Oil Plc were among those likely to bid for the licences, media reports said.
Each block covers 250 square metres and the initial rental fee will be 20 Irish pounds per square metre, giving a total cost of 5,000 punts a year.
